topStories.headline: Neighborhood Group 'Friends of Sunset Boulevard' Embroiled in Name-and-Mission Dispute
topStories.dek: A legal and community fight over who owns the identity — and the mailing list — of the eight-year-old beautification group has split the corridor's advocates.
topStories.body:
A community organization that spent years lobbying City Hall to beautify Sunset Boulevard has fractured into two rival factions, each now claiming the name 'Friends of Sunset Boulevard.' Co-founder Lorraine Patterson, who says she started the all-volunteer group in mid-2018 with neighbors on 36th Avenue, told the SF Standard that she is ceding the name after a rival faction incorporated as a nonprofit under the same name and sent her a cease-and-desist letter demanding she hand over the group's website, Instagram account, and distribution list.

The rival faction, which filed nonprofit paperwork with the California Secretary of State in March 2026, contends it has been actively executing on the group's original mission. In a public response, faction leader Lisa Arjes stated that the naming matter was settled on July 16, 2026 — ten days before the SF Standard story appeared — and that the incorporated nonprofit had already installed a native meadow pilot project, adopted the boulevard through the Department of Public Works Adopt-A-Street program, and removed more than a ton of trash from the median.

The dispute has drawn attention to broader questions about how Sunset Boulevard's greenbelt is managed. The corridor is overseen by the Department of Public Works rather than Recreation and Parks, and both factions have advocated for improvements. District 4 Supervisor Alan Wong has separately been working with Mayor Lurie's office to explore how Rec and Park can become involved in beautifying the boulevard.

topStories.headline: West Portal's Restaurant Boom Keeps Rolling With New Café in Former Hardware Store
topStories.dek: Hardware Coffee Co. opened in May 2026 inside the former Papenhausen Hardware building, adding another chapter to West Portal Avenue's emergence as a dining and café destination.
topStories.body:
West Portal Avenue, long considered a sleepy shopping strip, has quietly become one of San Francisco's most talked-about dining corridors — and the opening of Hardware Coffee Co. at 32 West Portal Ave. in May 2026 underscores just how fast things have changed. The all-day café, built into the space where Papenhausen Hardware operated for nearly a century, pairs premium coffee sourced from Oakland's Grand Coffee Roasters with beer, wine, and a full-service florist run by artist Sandra Bautista of Dasluz.

Owner Sam Pederson, a former tech worker who said the project is funded by his immediate family, told the San Francisco Chronicle the name is an homage to the hardware store predecessor and a statement about 'high quality, solid offerings, reliability and being part of the community.' Reviewers at The Infatuation described the two-story space as sun-drenched and airy, with an attached florist, standing room at an upstairs communal table, and a rotating lineup of seasonal slushies.

The opening fits a pattern the SF Standard described in June 2026: a West Portal restaurant boom that began with Little Original Joe's in 2020 and accelerated with the arrivals of Elena's Mexican Restaurant, Khao Tiew, Binu Bonu, and George's Donuts & Merriment. The Standard noted that the corridor had gone from 'stuck in 1985' to a neighborhood 'people go to on purpose to eat, even people who don't live there.'

topStories.headline: Inner Sunset Landmark Corner Gets New Life: Maggie & Mac's Open at 9th & Irving
topStories.dek: The long-vacant Social Kitchen & Brewery space on 9th Avenue finally has a new tenant, with the New American restaurant Maggie & Mac's opening in June to neighborhood fanfare.
topStories.body:
A corner that sat dark for more than six years has a heartbeat again. Maggie & Mac's, a New American restaurant and bar from Scott and Caitlyn Morton of the downtown institution MoMo's, opened at 1326 9th Ave. in June 2026, taking over the storefront that Social Kitchen & Brewery vacated in March 2020 when its operators and the landlord could not agree on a new lease.

The Richmond Review/Sunset Beacon, which covered the opening, described the restaurant as a place that 'feels less like an opening and more like a place that was always supposed to be in the neighborhood.' The Mortons have outfitted the two-story space with green and brown booths, wooden mezzanine tables, skylights, and a tucked-away back room called the Cable Car Room. The restaurant does not take reservations; all tables are first-come, first-served.

The Mortons have described their vision as 'a spot for weeknight burgers, Saturday negronis and Sunday hangs — a place for all the small moments that make a neighborhood feel like yours.' Maggie & Mac's is open Tuesday through Friday from noon to 9:30 p.m., Saturday from 11 a.m. to 9:30 p.m., and Sunday from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. The opening was widely watched as a signal of continued commercial momentum along the 9th and Irving corridor.

moreNews.headline: Shirley Chisholm Village Community Room Finally Opens to Public After Year-Long Wait
moreNews.body: A 749-square-foot community room at Shirley Chisholm Village — the 135-unit affordable housing complex for San Francisco teachers and school staff at 1360 43rd Ave. in the Outer Sunset — has been unlocked after sitting inaccessible for more than a year after the building's 2024 completion. Children's After School Arts (CASA) signed a lease in April 2026 to occupy the space as its 'CASA Clubhouse,' with a reservation system for public use launched on June 1. The room had been promised to the broader Outer Sunset community as a public gathering space, and its prolonged closure drew vocal criticism from local activists.

moreNews.headline: Supervisor Wong's Irish Cultural District Takes First Formal Steps
moreNews.body: The San Francisco Board of Supervisors voted unanimously on St. Patrick's Day 2026 to express the city's intent to establish an official Irish Cultural District in the Sunset neighborhood, following legislation introduced by District 4 Supervisor Alan Wong. Wong said the district would unlock $240,000 in funding to support the Irish community's cultural institutions and programming. A boundary committee is now conducting outreach with cultural leaders, residents, and small businesses to shape the district's formal boundaries and programming priorities.

moreNews.headline: Sunset Housing Market Runs Well Above Asking Price in 2026
moreNews.body: Homes across the Inner, Central, and Outer Sunset are closing at more than 130% of list price in 2026, with a median of just 12 days on market, according to a market report from Kinoko Real Estate published in late July 2026. Per-square-foot prices rose 5% to 8% year over year across all three sub-neighborhoods, with the Inner Sunset median sale price at roughly $2.23 million and the Outer Sunset at approximately $1.61 million as of early 2026. Real estate advisors note that Outer Sunset still offers the lowest absolute entry price of the three sub-markets, even as it appreciates at the fastest rate.
